passages.title: 환율 급변동 가격 전가 협의 메일
passages.passage:
From: Regional Pricing Director, EMEA
To: Country Managers
Subject: Currency Moves — Pricing Response Framework, Not Panic

Dear Country Managers,

The 12 percent currency swing over six weeks has generated a predictable inbox: every market wants either immediate price increases or permission to absorb the hit locally. Neither reflex serves us, so here is the framework the executive committee approved this morning.

First, contracts with currency adjustment clauses — roughly 40 percent of B2B revenue — execute per their terms, no discretion needed. Communicate early: customers forget signing these clauses and remember only the letter announcing them.

Second, list-price markets adjust in two steps of 4 to 5 percent, eight weeks apart, rather than one headline jump. Behavioral data from the last cycle is unambiguous: two moderate increases retained 30 percent more accounts than a single equivalent one, at trivial additional administrative cost.

Third — and this is the discipline point — no market may hold prices to gain share against sister markets. Cross-border customers arbitrage instantly; the gray-market flows from the last divergence took two years to unwind and poisoned three distributor relationships.

Hedging covers us through Q2, which buys deliberation, not delay. Country plans are due in ten days, and the pricing office will model each before any customer letter goes out.

Regards,
Sofia Lindgren

questions.q: What must markets with adjustment clauses do?
choices: Execute per contract terms and communicate early
questions.exKo: 조항대로 집행하되 고객이 잊고 있으므로 일찍 안내하라고 지시합니다.

questions.q: Why are two-step increases preferred?
choices: They retained far more accounts than single jumps
questions.exKo: 지난 사이클에서 두 번의 완만한 인상이 고객 유지율 30% 우위를 보였습니다.

questions.q: Why is holding prices to gain share forbidden?
questions.exKo: 국경 간 재정거래와 회색시장 유통이 관계를 해치고 수년간 후유증을 남기기 때문입니다.

passages.title: 품질 사고 고객사 브리핑 메일
passages.passage:
From: VP Quality, Meridian Components
To: Quality Directors, Key Accounts
Subject: Batch 7A Deviation — Full Technical Disclosure

Dear Quality Directors,

You will have received our formal deviation notice yesterday. This letter adds what formal notices cannot: the complete technical picture, including what we do not yet know.

What happened: a torque sensor on line 3 drifted out of calibration between routine checks, and 4,100 units shipped with fastener torque potentially 8 percent below specification. Drift was caught by the statistical monitoring we installed after last year's incident — the system worked, but the detection lag means three weeks of production is in scope.

What we know: accelerated life testing on retained samples shows no failures through 120 percent of rated cycles. What we do not know: whether your specific application profiles — particularly high-vibration installations — narrow that margin. We would rather say this plainly than have you discover a gap between our confidence and our evidence.

Our proposal: units in your inventory can be returned for retorquing at our cost with 72-hour turnaround, or — for installations where removal costs exceed the part's value — our field engineers will verify torque in place using calibrated equipment, documented per unit. Your choice per site; both paths carry full warranty extension.

My direct line is below. The engineers who found the drift are available for technical calls this week — you will get answers from the people with the data, not from a script.

Dr. Emil Hartmann

questions.q: How was the calibration drift discovered?
choices: Statistical monitoring installed after a prior incident
questions.exKo: 작년 사고 후 도입한 통계적 모니터링이 감지했습니다.

questions.q: What does the company admit not knowing?
choices: Whether high-vibration applications narrow the safety margin
questions.exKo: 고진동 환경에서 여유 마진이 줄어드는지는 아직 모른다고 인정합니다.

questions.q: What choice do customers have per site?
choices: Return for retorquing or on-site verified torque checks
questions.exKo: 반품 재체결 또는 현장 토크 검증 중 선택할 수 있으며 모두 보증이 연장됩니다.

passages.title: 해외 파견 근무 제도 개편 공지
passages.passage:
INTERNATIONAL ASSIGNMENT PROGRAM — REDESIGN

The expatriate program has been redesigned following a review of 60 assignments over five years. The findings were sobering enough to share: a third of assignments ended early, repatriated employees left the company at twice the average rate within 18 months, and assignment costs averaged 2.4 times home salary while measured knowledge transfer — the program's stated purpose — occurred in fewer than half of cases.

The diagnosis was structural. Assignments were treated as rewards and staffed by availability; success was measured by completion, not outcomes; and repatriation was an afterthought — returning employees came back to roles that ignored their new capabilities, which explains the attrition better than any exit interview.

The redesigned program inverts each failure. Assignments now begin with a written capability-transfer objective and a named receiving successor — no successor identified, no assignment approved. Duration follows the objective, with 6-to-12-month targeted assignments replacing the default three years. And repatriation planning starts at month one: the returning role is agreed in writing before departure, revisited quarterly, and the sponsoring executive is accountable for honoring it.

Fewer assignments will be approved under these rules, deliberately. A smaller program that transfers capability beats a larger one that transfers households.

Applications for the first cycle open Monday on the mobility portal.

Global Mobility Office

questions.q: What did the five-year review find?
choices: High early termination, post-return attrition, and weak knowledge transfer
questions.exKo: 조기 종료 3분의 1, 복귀 후 이직 2배, 지식 이전 절반 미만이라는 결과였습니다.

questions.q: What now blocks an assignment's approval?
questions.exKo: 역량을 이어받을 후임자가 지정되지 않으면 파견이 승인되지 않습니다.

questions.q: What explains post-return attrition, per the notice?
choices: Returning roles ignored newly built capabilities
questions.exKo: 복귀 보직이 새 역량을 무시했다는 것이 이직의 실제 원인이었습니다.

passages.title: 제보 기반 품질 보상 프로그램 공지
passages.passage:
QUALITY CATCH PROGRAM — PAYING FOR BAD NEWS

Starting next month, the company will pay for defect discoveries — a policy that deserves explanation, because paying employees to find problems strikes some managers as paying for failure.

The economics are the opposite. Our cost-of-quality data is unambiguous: a defect caught at the workstation costs one unit of correction; the same defect at final inspection costs ten; at a customer site, one hundred and a relationship. Any incentive that moves discovery earlier is self-funding at almost any price.

The program: any employee who identifies and documents a previously unknown defect source — not an instance, a source — receives a graded award from $200 to $5,000, scaled by the exposure prevented. The distinction matters: reporting a scratched housing is your job; tracing scratches to a worn conveyor guide that has been marking one unit in forty for a month is a catch, and it pays.

Two rules protect the program's integrity. Awards attach to discovery, not blame — a catch in your own area pays identically, and no catch triggers discipline for the area where it was found; the previous culture of quiet fixes was rational under blame, and we are pricing the rationality out. Second, the quality team validates catches within five days, and disputed calls escalate to a cross-functional panel whose decisions publish monthly, anonymized.

Last year's informal pilots surfaced 23 systemic issues. We suspect that was a fraction of what walks past us daily.

Quality Directorate

questions.q: What justifies paying for defect discoveries?
questions.exKo: 발견 시점이 빠를수록 시정 비용이 1:10:100으로 낮아져 자체 회수됩니다.

questions.q: What qualifies as a 'catch'?
choices: Identifying a defect source, not just an instance
questions.exKo: 긁힌 제품 신고가 아니라 마모된 가이드라는 '원인'을 찾아야 보상 대상입니다.

questions.q: Why do catches carry no discipline for the affected area?
choices: Blame made hiding problems rational, and the program prices that out
questions.exKo: 비난 문화에서는 조용히 덮는 것이 합리적이었기에 그 유인을 제거하는 것입니다.

passages.title: 기업 탄소 회계 플랫폼 광고
passages.passage:
CARBONLEDGER — EMISSIONS ACCOUNTING THAT SURVIVES AN AUDIT

Your sustainability report is about to meet your auditor. The spreadsheet estimates and supplier questionnaires that satisfied voluntary disclosure will not satisfy assurance standards written for financial rigor — and restating emissions is tomorrow's restating earnings.

CarbonLedger applies accounting discipline to carbon. Every emission figure traces to a source document — utility invoice, fuel receipt, freight manifest — through an audit trail your assurance provider can walk line by line. Estimation, where unavoidable, is flagged as estimation, with methodology, uncertainty range, and a replacement plan as actuals arrive; auditors tell us the honest uncertainty labeling shortens their fieldwork more than any feature.

Supplier data — the swamp where most programs sink — is handled with tiered rigor: invoiced actuals from your largest emitters, verified averages for the middle tier, and modeled estimates below, each tier labeled and weighted so improvement resources target the tonnage that matters. Year-on-year comparisons stay valid through methodology changes via restatement bridges, the same discipline your finance team applies to accounting policy shifts.

Built by former Big Four assurance practitioners who kept the skepticism and lost the billable hours. Implementation in one quarter; assurance-readiness assessment free at carbonledger.com/ready.

questions.q: What problem does the ad predict?
choices: Voluntary-grade emissions data failing formal assurance
questions.exKo: 자발적 공시 수준의 데이터가 회계 수준 검증을 통과하지 못하는 상황을 경고합니다.

questions.q: How does the platform treat unavoidable estimates?
choices: Flags them with methodology, uncertainty, and replacement plans
questions.exKo: 추정치임을 명시하고 방법론·불확실성·실측 대체 계획을 붙입니다.

questions.q: How is supplier data organized?
choices: Tiered rigor weighted by emission significance
questions.exKo: 배출 비중에 따라 실측·검증 평균·모델 추정으로 계층화합니다.

passages.title: 경영권 승계 가족기업 자문 광고
passages.passage:
THIRDGEN ADVISORS — FAMILY BUSINESS TRANSITIONS WITHOUT THE FAMILY BREAKING

The statistics are famous: most family businesses do not survive the second generational handover. The reasons are less discussed, because they are uncomfortable: succession fails on dinner-table grievances long before it fails on estate taxes.

ThirdGen works both ledgers. Our advisors pair a transaction specialist with a family-systems facilitator, because the recapitalization structure means nothing if the non-operating siblings feel bought off, and the family harmony means nothing if the buyout terms bankrupt the operating heir. We have seen technically perfect transitions collapse over a vacation-home clause; we now ask about the vacation home in meeting one.

Our process starts with individual conversations — every stakeholder, including in-laws with no shares and considerable influence — before any group session. The output is a transition charter covering ownership, employment rules for family members, dividend policy, and dispute resolution, signed before the legal documents that implement it. Charters do not prevent disagreement; they convert 'you always favored her' into 'section four says.'

Fees are fixed per phase and disclosed fully — a family in transition does not need an adviser with hourly incentives to prolong conflict. Engagements begin with a no-cost readiness conversation, in strict confidence, at thirdgen.family.

questions.q: Why do successions fail, per the ad?
choices: Family grievances more than technical structuring
questions.exKo: 상속세보다 가족 내 해묵은 감정이 승계를 무너뜨린다는 진단입니다.

questions.q: Why are in-laws without shares interviewed?
choices: They hold influence despite having no ownership
questions.exKo: 지분은 없어도 상당한 영향력을 갖기 때문입니다.

questions.q: What does the transition charter accomplish?
choices: Converts emotional disputes into reference to agreed rules
questions.exKo: 감정적 비난을 '4조에 따르면'이라는 규칙 준거로 바꿔 줍니다.

passages.title: 직무기술서 무용론과 스킬 채용 기사
passages.passage:
TALENT STRATEGY — The degree requirement is quietly disappearing from job postings, but researchers tracking the shift report a subtler finding: removing credentials changed who applied far more than it changed who was hired.

Across 1,100 postings studied by a labor economics group, dropping degree requirements lifted applications from non-traditional candidates by 40 percent — yet hiring outcomes for those candidates improved only where companies also rebuilt their assessment process. Where interviews still ran on unstructured conversation, familiar proxies crept back: interviewers favored candidates who resembled previous hires, credential or not. 'You cannot remove a filter and keep the plumbing that needed it,' the study's lead author observed.

The organizations showing genuine change share mechanics: work-sample assessments scored blind before any interview, structured interviews with anchored rating scales, and — the strongest predictor — hiring manager scorecards audited against subsequent job performance, closing the loop that most talent systems leave open. One logistics firm rebuilt its dispatcher hiring around a simulation of an actual chaotic Tuesday; first-year retention rose 25 percent, and the profile of successful hires shifted visibly toward career changers.

The report's conclusion is unsentimental: skills-based hiring is not a posting edit but an assessment rebuild, and companies doing the former while skipping the latter harvest applications they are not equipped to evaluate.

questions.q: What did removing degree requirements change most?
choices: Who applied, more than who was hired
questions.exKo: 지원자 구성은 크게 바뀌었지만 채용 결과는 평가 개편 없이는 달라지지 않았습니다.

questions.q: What was the strongest predictor of genuine change?
choices: Auditing hiring scorecards against later job performance
questions.exKo: 채용 평가와 이후 실제 성과를 대조 검증하는 피드백 루프였습니다.

questions.q: What is the report's core conclusion?
choices: Skills-based hiring requires rebuilding assessment, not editing postings
questions.exKo: 공고 문구 수정이 아니라 평가 체계 재구축이 본질이라는 결론입니다.

passages.title: 전력 다소비 산업의 입지 이동 기사
passages.passage:
ENERGY ECONOMICS — Electricity has replaced labor as the site-selection variable that ends negotiations, and the map of heavy industry is redrawing accordingly. Aluminum smelters, hydrogen electrolyzers, and data centers — projects whose power bills dwarf their payrolls — are clustering where grids offer three increasingly scarce commodities: available capacity, price stability, and interconnection dates measured in months rather than years.

The sorting is already visible in project announcements. Regions with surplus hydropower report industrial inquiries at five times historical rates, while two long-dominant manufacturing corridors have lost marquee projects over interconnection queues alone — capacity existed on paper, but four-year connection timelines function as rejection. 'The grid connection is the new building permit,' one site consultant remarked, 'except no mayor can expedite it.'

Second-order effects are emerging. Power-rich regions have begun negotiating like the resource owners they are: several now condition industrial tariffs on local hiring thresholds, apprenticeship funding, or waste-heat delivery to district systems — terms once associated with mineral concessions. Meanwhile, projects are redesigning themselves around grid reality: modular plants sized to available capacity, on-site generation hybrids, and — in a reversal that would have puzzled a previous generation — factories sited first and markets served second, with logistics costs absorbed as the price of watts.

Analysts caution the clustering carries concentration risk: a drought year in a hydro-dependent region now ripples through global commodity chains that quietly co-located there.

questions.q: What has become the decisive site-selection factor?
choices: Electricity capacity, stability, and connection speed
questions.exKo: 전력 가용량·가격 안정성·연결 속도가 입지를 결정짓고 있습니다.

questions.q: How do long interconnection queues function?
choices: As effective rejections despite paper capacity
questions.exKo: 서류상 용량이 있어도 4년 대기는 사실상 거절로 작용합니다.

questions.q: How are power-rich regions behaving?
choices: Attaching resource-owner conditions to industrial tariffs
questions.exKo: 현지 고용, 폐열 공급 등 자원 보유국식 조건을 요금에 결부시키고 있습니다.

passages.title: 특허 침해 경고장 대응 문자
passages.passage:
Rita Yoon (11:05 A.M.)
We received a cease-and-desist on the conveyor tensioning feature. Patent holder is Dynatech. Board call in 3 hours — I need our position.

Steve Karlin (11:12 A.M.)
Read it. Three observations before anyone panics. One: their claim construction stretches — our tensioner adjusts continuously, their patent claims discrete stepped adjustment. Counsel sees a solid non-infringement argument.

Rita Yoon (11:14 A.M.)
Two?

Steve Karlin (11:16 A.M.)
Two: our archives show we demonstrated continuous tensioning at the Hannover fair 14 months before their filing date. If the demo covered the claimed elements, that's invalidating prior art — the video and the sales brochure are already with counsel.

Rita Yoon (11:18 A.M.)
And three?

Steve Karlin (11:20 A.M.)
Three: context. Dynatech sent identical letters to four competitors last quarter — this is licensing revenue harvesting, not litigation appetite. They settled with two at modest per-unit royalties. Their pattern says they avoid trial.

Rita Yoon (11:23 A.M.)
So the board options: fight on non-infringement plus prior art, or negotiate from that strength toward a nominal license?

Steve Karlin (11:26 A.M.)
Exactly — and the sequencing matters. Respond with the prior art documented but not yet filed for invalidation. It signals we can end their whole licensing program, which makes a cheap walk-away license attractive to them. Filing immediately burns that leverage for everyone they've already licensed.

Rita Yoon (11:27 A.M.)
That's the memo. Send me the Hannover evidence summary by 1?

Steve Karlin (11:28 A.M.)
With the claim chart. You'll have both.

questions.q: What is the non-infringement argument?
choices: Continuous adjustment differs from the patent's stepped claims
questions.exKo: 특허는 단계식 조절을 청구하는데 자사 제품은 연속 조절이라는 차이입니다.

questions.q: Why is the Hannover demonstration important?
choices: It may be invalidating prior art predating the filing
It shows the patent copied them
questions.exKo: 출원 14개월 전 공개 시연이라 특허 무효화 선행기술이 될 수 있습니다.

questions.q: Why hold the prior art without filing immediately?
choices: The threat of ending their licensing program buys a cheap settlement
questions.exKo: 무효화 위협 자체가 협상 지렛대이며, 즉시 제기하면 그 레버리지를 소진합니다.

passages.title: 대규모 세일 기간 사기 거래 대응 문자
passages.passage:
Omar Aziz (8:40 P.M.)
Fraud dashboard just went orange. Chargeback-prone patterns tripled in the last hour — mostly high-value electronics to freshly created accounts.

Lena Marsh (8:43 P.M.)
Sale night brings both crowds. What's the false-positive cost if we tighten the rules now?

Omar Aziz (8:45 P.M.)
That's the tension. Aggressive filtering tonight blocks maybe 400 fraudulent orders but declines an estimated 900 legitimate ones — new customers buying gifts look statistically identical to mules for the first 24 hours.

Lena Marsh (8:48 P.M.)
Declining 900 real first-time buyers on sale night is brand damage we'll pay for all year. Middle path?

Omar Aziz (8:50 P.M.)
Hold-and-verify tier: suspicious orders neither approved nor declined — held 12 hours with a soft email, 'confirming your order details.' Fraudsters abandon at 80 percent when fulfillment stalls; legitimate buyers overwhelmingly confirm. We lose speed, not customers.

Lena Marsh (8:52 P.M.)
Inventory implication? Held units are locked during our biggest sell-through window.

Omar Aziz (8:54 P.M.)
Capped at 3 percent of sale inventory, released on decision. And one addition: exclude the hold tier from next-day delivery promises automatically — better no promise than a broken one.

Lena Marsh (8:55 P.M.)
Approved. Route the hold queue to the overnight review team, and I want the abandonment stats at 9 A.M. — if the 80 percent holds, this becomes standard sale-night playbook.

Omar Aziz (8:56 P.M.)
Deploying now.

questions.q: Why not simply tighten fraud rules?
choices: It would decline many legitimate new customers
questions.exKo: 400건 차단 대가로 정상 신규 주문 900건이 거절되기 때문입니다.

questions.q: How does hold-and-verify separate fraudsters?
choices: Fraudsters mostly abandon when fulfillment stalls
questions.exKo: 처리가 지연되면 사기범의 80%는 포기하지만 정상 고객은 확인에 응합니다.

questions.q: Why exclude held orders from next-day delivery promises?
choices: An unmade promise beats a broken one
questions.exKo: 지키지 못할 약속을 하지 않는 편이 낫다는 판단입니다.
